So what happened to all these tall skeletons that were dug up?

The authors think they have traced some back to the Carnegies and have found evidence that others were sold - like many other antiquities of the time - to wealthy US families. Other skeletons turned to chalk where they laid due to erosion. The authors do more than acknowledge the many newspaper clippings and county register entries, which in addition to oral traditions tell a pretty convincing tale. They dug further into Smithsonian reports, Buearu of Ethnology reports, and the field notebooks of the very agents who noted the size and shape of these skeletons, and in some instances used the verbiage, "gigantic human" to describe the finds. Oddly some of the field notebook entries, like much of the published research conducted by Smithsonian agents before the reign of Ales Hrdlicka was altered in subsequent reports - not only the size of the skeletons, but the shapes of adjacent earthworks as well. Why would this entrusted institution find and document these beings (17 total if i'm not mistaken), then claim that all their field agents didn't know how to measure? That's pretty tough to believe, especially since one - Col. Norris - was a high ranking official in the US Army.
There are many who claim all the giant skeleton reports were hoaxes, and some were. The question is, did the Smithsonian lie about finding the giant skeletons, or lie when they documented the finds?

Theres plenty of people over 7 feet tall today, shit the best man in my wedding is 6'9 ( which is funny because im only 5'7 ) but what is the supposed signifcance of this?

The average height back then was 5', and these beings were venerated - buried underneath mounds, adorned, honored. The mounds they were found beneath are exactly like ancient European Bell Barrows, right down to the details of the "A" frame structure in the interior surrounded by other burials. The skulls from the notebooks have been recreated by Marcia K Moore, some have European facial features and some elongated skulls. Aside from the fact that these beings existed, the most compelling thing to me is that the Smithsonian has kept this research from us for more than 100 years - why? They claim all of their agents mis-measured, which as a sentient human is difficult for me to buy - especially since one was Col. Norris of the US Army. They either lied when they documented all these skeletons, or they've lied ever since - either way it doesn't make me feel all warm and fuzzy to know this. If they're lying about this, what other important research from our past has been kept from us?
